transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; what brings you in to see me today?

Hi Dr. Smith. It's really nice to meet you too. Thank you so much for having me. 

Um... well, I guess what finally made me schedule an appointment is... it's a little embarrassing, honestly, and it's probably not the worst thing in the world, but I keep making these silly little mistakes. Like, I'll turn in applications or my research notes, and there will be these small errors—maybe a mislabeled artwork date, or I'll just completely skip a question. And the weird part is, I honestly thought I had checked them over really carefully before submitting them. 

It's just a bit frustrating to keep doing that when I'm really trying my best. I hope I'm explaining that right? Is that the kind of thing I should be starting with?
Do you find that you spend a significant amount of your day feeling uncontrollably worried or anxious about things in general, beyond just these specific mistakes?

Oh, no, definitely not. Um, I hope I didn't make it sound like I'm, you know, falling apart or anything! I'm actually a pretty upbeat person most of the time. 

I don't really sit around worrying about life in general. It's... it's honestly just the frustration with myself over those specific mistakes. Like, I just want to do a good job and be reliable, you know? So, no, no uncontrollable anxiety or anything like that. Just... a little annoyance at myself when I mess up. 

Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information.

When you check your work over, are you doing it because you feel a strong, repetitive urge to make sure everything is perfect to prevent something bad from happening, or is it more that you are trying to catch those small errors you mentioned?

Oh, um, definitely just trying to catch the errors. It's not like a... a compulsion or anything intense like that. I just know I have a tendency to miss things, so I try to be extra careful and look it over before I hand it in. 

I'm not worried about anything terrible happening, I just... I don't want to look careless to my professors, you know? I really do care about my work. I just want to make sure I'm doing things right. Is that... is that the normal reason people double-check things?
When you are working on your research or other tasks, do you often find it difficult to sustain your attention until you finish the project?

Um, well, I guess sometimes my mind wanders a little bit? But I think that's pretty normal, right? Like, if I'm reading a really dry paper for a class, it might take me a little longer to get through it than I'd like, and I might need to take a few breaks. 

But I wouldn't say it's, like, a huge problem or anything. I always get my projects done on time. I just... maybe I have to work a little harder at staying focused than some people? I'm not really sure. I mean, everyone gets a little distracted sometimes, don't they? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is. I really do try to stay on track.
Do you often feel like you have an internal motor that keeps you moving, or do you find that you frequently interrupt others when they are talking?

Oh, um, no, definitely not. I don't feel like I'm constantly moving or anything like that. I can sit still perfectly fine! And I really try hard not to interrupt people. I always want to be polite and let others finish what they're saying before I chime in. 

I think I'm a pretty good listener, actually. I'd hate to make anyone feel like I was talking over them or being rude. So, no, I don't think I do either of those things. Is that... I hope that's helpful? I just want to make sure I'm answering exactly what you're looking for.
Do you often find that you struggle to keep your personal belongings or workspace organized, or do you frequently lose things that you need for your daily tasks?

Um, well, I wouldn't say I *frequently* lose things... I mean, I usually find them eventually! But, I guess my organization could maybe be a little better? 

Like, if you looked at my apartment or my laptop right now, it might seem a bit... cluttered? It's just that I get really involved in things. So there are rent papers, gallery notes, some article PDFs, and, like, half-finished to-do lists kind of scattered around. It looks like a bunch of half-started projects, I suppose. 

I just sometimes have a little trouble figuring out what actually needs to happen first, so everything kind of stays out where I can see it. But I wouldn't call it a huge struggle or anything. A lot of college students are a little messy, right? I mean, I'm definitely working on being neater. I hope that doesn't make me sound too disorganized?
Looking back at when you were a child—in elementary or middle school—did you often have these same struggles with making careless mistakes or feeling a bit disorganized?

Um, well... I guess I was a little bit like that when I was younger, too? But I think a lot of kids are, right? 

Like, I remember in elementary school, my teachers would always write on my report cards that I had really good ideas. They always said that! But, um, they might also mention that I sometimes... forgot to turn in my worksheets? Or that I'd misplace the instructions for an assignment. And maybe I missed some little details here and there. 

It wasn't terrible, though! My parents just had to check my backpack every night to make sure everything was in there. Once they did that, everything was totally fine. I mean, it's pretty normal for kids to need a little help from their parents with that kind of stuff, isn't it? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of examples. I was a really good kid, I promise!

Do you feel that these challenges with organization and attention have ever caused you significant problems in your personal life or academic progress, or do you feel you are able to manage them well enough on your own?

Um, well, I wouldn't say they cause *significant* problems... I mean, I'm still doing okay! I guess, um, maybe it has caused a few little hiccups here and there? 

Like, because I sometimes get a bit disorganized with the PDFs and the notes, I've... well, I've submitted a couple of assignments a little late. And, um, I might have missed a deadline or two for some applications I was really hoping to do. But I'm sure I can just apply again next time! 

I did have a mentor recently mention that my, um, my follow-through was maybe starting to hurt some opportunities that I should be ready for. Which, you know, wasn't great to hear. I really want to do a good job and impress them! So I'm definitely trying to be more on top of things now so that doesn't happen again. 

I'm managing it the best I can, though! I hope that doesn't make me sound like a bad student or anything? I really do care about my work a lot.

Beyond the mistakes and organization issues we've discussed, do you often find that you struggle to keep your mind on what you are doing during conversations or while reading, or do you frequently find yourself avoiding tasks that require a lot of sustained mental effort?

Um, well... I definitely wouldn't say I avoid things completely! I always get my work done eventually, I promise. It's just that, um, sometimes... I guess if I know something is going to take a really, really long time to focus on? Like, um, drafting a curatorial proposal or having to read one of those really dense art theory chapters... 

I might, um, I might just decide to do some smaller, easier errands first? Just to kind of warm up, you know? Like, I'll organize my desk or answer some quick emails. And then, well, sometimes those little things take longer than I thought, and... suddenly it's the night before the big project is due, and I haven't really started the hard part yet. 

But I always finish it before the deadline! Well, usually. I just work really well under pressure, I think? A lot of people do that, right? Procrastinate just a little bit when something is really heavy? I just want to make sure I'm not making it sound worse than it is... I really do try my best to stay focused when I need to!
